anti_generic_signature_read: 'The underlying format is generic: a square grid, two colours of base, pieces with rank numbers. That's chess's skeleton... What is *not* generic is the commitment to making every piece a specific, recognisable, individually-textured little world rather than an abstract token -- and the fact that the pieces are different *sizes* from each other in a way that appears to track something real about the subjects, rather than being uniform for ergonomics. Mass-market games almost always make pieces the same size for handling.' Most memorable thing in the frame, chosen unprompted: 'the small grey ball with the orange ring-and-white-centre mark. It's the smallest, plainest-coloured piece on the board and it's the one whose surface actually made me stop and look. Every other ball is a colour scheme; that one is a *map*.'
blind_action_read: 'Nothing is moving; these are static renders. But they are not the same thing.' A is 'a single isometric view of the board fully populated -- all sixteen balls on the board -- with the two empty trays floating beside it'. B is 'a strip of three panels showing the same board in three different states. The terrain is identical in all three... What changes is the balls. Panel 1 has all sixteen. Panel 2 has about twelve, and they are on *different cells* than in panel 1. Panel 3 has about six or seven, on different cells again. So B reads as a sequence: pieces moving and being removed, a game progressing from a full opening position toward a thinned-out endgame.'
blind_form_read: 'One dominant mass: a thin rectangular slab, wider than deep, with a plain raised border rim framing an inner field of square cells... The slab is maybe 1/15th as thick as it is long; it reads as a tray or plaque, not a box.' On it, 'a scatter of small vertical masses: each ball is roughly 60-80% of a cell in diameter and sits on a squat cylindrical disc a little under one cell wide.' Unprompted: 'The balls are *not* all one size -- there is a clear size hierarchy. The banded gas giant and the ringed one are the largest (nearly a full cell wide); the blue and cyan ones are mid-sized; the red one, the white plumed one and the grey speckled one are visibly the smallest, maybe half the diameter of the largest.' Terrain is 'set *into* the slab, flush or recessed below the top face', in two 2x3 blocks of twelve brown tiles plus an orange 2x2 group and a cyan 2x2 group.
blind_held_read: A board game. 'A flat rectangular grey slab is divided into a regular grid of square cells; sixteen coloured balls, each seated on its own round disc-shaped foot, are distributed across it; certain cells are sunk and filled with coloured textured terrain; small cones stand at the corners of those terrain cells; and two separate grey trays with moulded pockets sit off to one side, evidently to hold the balls when not in play.' Named unprompted in three words as 'planet checkers board', because 'the balls are unmistakably styled as planets (a banded gas giant with a red oval; a ringed yellow one; a blue-and-green one with white caps)'.
blind_relationship_read: 'The board is the reference frame, everything else locates against it. Each ball is permanently married to its disc... That unit occupies one grid cell. Terrain tiles *are* cells -- they replace ordinary cells rather than sitting on them, so terrain is fixed and pieces are mobile.' Function read unprompted: 'a two-player territorial or capture game. The eight-designs-times-two structure, with one set on white feet and one on black feet, is the giveaway: two players, eight identical piece types each, distinguished only by base colour, exactly as in chess or shogi. The engraved digits on the bases suggest each type has a rank or value.' The trays are 'clearly the off-board reservoir'.
blind_subjects_read: Enumerated piece by piece, unprompted: one board slab; two trays with ten pockets each; 'sixteen base discs: eight white, eight black', each with 'one small engraved glyph on its vertical rim'; and 'sixteen balls, in eight designs, each design appearing exactly twice (once on a white disc, once on a black disc)' -- a ringed pale-yellow sphere; a banded orange sphere with 'one solid dark red oval blob'; a blue sphere with white bands and a 'small grey oval spot'; a cyan sphere with 'a single broad white stripe running pole to pole'; a blue-green sphere that 'reads as a globe of Earth'; a white sphere with an orange mark; a red sphere with 'irregular khaki/tan patches'; and 'the smallest ball. Grey body, several irregular orange patches, and one orange patch that is a ring with a white centre.' Terrain: twelve recessed brown cratered tiles, three orange and three cyan engraved sunburst tiles, one cream plate standing proud, one plain black tile, and sixteen cones.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Unprompted, before knowing which piece mattered or that it had ever been featureless: 'the ring marking is clear as a small orange dot with a bright white pinprick in the middle -- about 17 px for the orange, about 11 px for the white core. So the presence of a bright centre inside an orange spot does survive to A.' On re-measurement the critic located pure-white cores at (384.6, 572.6) and (1505.7, 582.3) in iso.png -- the two Mercury globes -- at 18% of the globe's diameter.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Both Mercury pieces show a surface marking a reader can point at in the canonical whole-set render, not only in the close-ups.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Named as a basin blind, with no prompt and no product name: 'One marking is an annulus -- an orange ring enclosing a distinctly different, brighter, pure-white core... the only marking on the piece with any internal structure.' Asked what it depicts, unprompted: 'A large impact crater -- the orange ring being the raised rim or ejecta blanket, the pale core being the crater floor... a single named basin far larger than anything else on the surface is the obvious reading.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mercury carries a large ringed impact basin: a bright interior inside a distinct rim, reading as a basin rather than as a painted dot.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Detected blind on both Mercury globes in iso.png, and on both in signature.png panel 1 (blobs at 264.3,333.1 and 932.1,410.2) and panel 2 (397.7,493.6 and 464.7,371.3). Panel 3 carries no Mercury piece, so the requirement does not arise there.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The basin is on the camera-facing hemisphere at both frames the product is photographed from, on both armies.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Catalogued blind, before knowing a union of circles was the defect being corrected: 'So: one circle, everything else irregular. That contrast is exactly what makes the ring read as a different kind of feature.' Individually: 'a lopsided blob with a bulge on one side'; 'kidney- or teardrop-shaped'; 'strongly irregular. Distinctly lobed.' The single circle is the basin itself.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mercury's smooth plains are irregular lobed shapes, not circles.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'One large lobed patch across the lower centre, shaped like a peanut or a figure-of-eight, and much bigger than anything on the other side -- about 60% of the ball's diameter across. It is the single largest marking on the piece... two rounded masses joined by a waist, like a peanut, with a small tail off one end.' Re-measured at 14,453 px against 4,128 and 2,473 for the next two patches on that face.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Two or three plains run together into one larger smooth-plain region.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'The body itself is a neutral light grey.' Sampled (225,226,225) lit through (158,159,158) mid-tone, R=G=B to within 1.

Blind and numeric, before knowing the two were meant to match: 'The same pattern, identically... in D the orange covers 12,105 pixels with a bounding box from x=299 to x=603; in E it covers 12,020 pixels with a bounding box from x=299 to x=602. Those are the same object in the same pose, to within antialiasing.' The critic also proved the two polar frames differ by a 180-degree image-plane rotation, by mapping all four patch centroids through (x,y)->(898-x,898-y) -- a camera azimuth difference, not a handedness in the parts.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The two Mercury pieces remain exact mirrors of one another -- the same world, with only the ownership cue inverted.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind, without computing anything: 'The balls are not all one size -- there is a clear size hierarchy... the red one, the white plumed one and the grey speckled one are visibly the smallest', and of Mercury, 'The smallest ball.' On re-measurement against a single scale anchor, all eight globes land within 0.6 mm of the fifth-root prediction and the order is monotonic with Mercury smallest of all sixteen.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mercury is still the smallest globe in the set and the measured rank ladder still reads.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'twelve brown cratered tiles in two 2x3 blocks', 'three recessed orange sunburst tiles plus one raised cream plate', 'three recessed cyan sunburst tiles plus one flat black tile', 'two identical grey rectangular trays, each with ten shallow scalloped pockets', and the function read as 'two players, eight identical piece types each, distinguished only by base colour'. On re-measurement the field is 7 columns by 9 rows, water at columns 2-3 and 5-6 of rows 4-6, dens at column 4 rows 1 and 9, traps at columns 3 and 5 of both end rows plus column 4 of rows 2 and 8.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The rest of the set still reads as a playable Dou Shou Qi set: a 7x9 field, an impassable belt across the middle, a den at each end with flanking traps, and off-board storage.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind, in the critic's own words and unprompted: 'They read as terrain -- material of a different colour. Not as holes, not as gaps, not as dents, and not as failed print.' With the reason measured rather than asserted: 'the orange patches darken and lighten across the sphere in exact step with the grey body' -- (213,144,45) lit against (157,106,33) at the limb -- 'and in F and G, where the whole visible face is turned away from the light, the patches go uniformly darker brown along with everything else rather than staying bright. That is a coloured surface, not an absence of one.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: the darkened terrain must read as terrain, not as a hole, gap, dent or failed print.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind, the critic catalogued six or seven markings and every one is a large blob, crescent or lobed region; not one small crater appears anywhere in the phase-one record. On re-measurement at a deliberately loose threshold across all six single-piece views, the substantial features are 5253/4766/4248/1036 px on the basin face, 14578/4158/2478 px on the far face and 6341/5181/2661/442/224 px on the polar face, and 'everything else is 1-22 px, which is antialiasing fringe along the edges of those same large patches, not discrete marks.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: no crater field -- no scatter of small craters anywhere on either Mercury piece.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: No bump, relief or protrusion appears anywhere in the phase-one record. On re-measurement the critic fitted a circle to the Mercury silhouette (radius 164 px, centre 449.5,352) and tested it where one orange patch runs down the right limb, spanning y 256-388 -- the place any relief would bulge the outline: predicted against measured widths agree to within one pixel at y=236, 268, 300, 436, 452 and 460. 'The inlay is flush.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: nothing protrudes from Mercury's globe -- no relief, no raised feature, no bump; the silhouette stays a clean sphere.

largest_risk: Two requirements the images cannot settle, both disclosed and both settled instead by measurement on the solids. The critic answered CANNOT-JUDGE-FROM-IMAGES to each and was right to. First, whether any downward-facing surface was added to Mercury: every close-up looks down on the piece, so a downward face is geometrically invisible in this image set. It is settled by the print gate and by the byte comparison -- check_overhang reports 0 unsupported samples over 0 regions on both Mercury parts at a 45 degree limit, and measure/revision-part-hashes.md shows part_world_mercury_sol.step and part_world_mercury_anti.step byte-identical to the set this corrects, so the printed solid did not move at all and no surface of any orientation was added. Second, whether anything outside the two Mercury pieces changed: the critic has no previous build to difference against. measure/occurrence-geometry.md answers it -- 152 labels identical in solid count, exact volume and bounding box, and 'Nothing outside mercury_sol_* and mercury_anti_* gained, lost or moved a solid.' Beyond those, the honest ceiling on this evidence: the basin's floor clamps to flat white in the review renderer, so at whole-set scale it reads as a bright dot rather than as a floor inside a rim -- the marking is unmistakably there, which is what this correction had to achieve, but its ring structure is only legible in the per-world frames. Nothing here has been printed, handled or played.
resolution: The blind read confirmed every positive and negative held-form requirement the images can carry; no repair round was needed. The critic's ten phase-one findings were each answered by measurement. Three it withdrew itself on re-measuring: a cone through a globe (the flame tip clears Mercury's crown by ~33 px, its body hidden behind), discs overhanging cells (33.3 mm of disc in a 36.3 mm cell), and the den being oversized or misplaced (its top face is inset within its cell and dead-centre once its 2.20 mm raise is corrected for). Three more were settled here. Saturn's ring appearing to overhang its base is projection: the part's own bounding box is X and Y -16.937..16.937 mm, exactly its disc's widest radius, so nothing reaches past its own disc, and inspect interfere on the whole 186-occurrence assembly reports clashCount 0 over 298 boolean-tested pairs, which answers the ring-through-ball and ring-through-base readings together. The two dens differing in height is impossible: measure/occurrence-geometry.md shows them as one geometry instanced twice, 2 solids under a single label with Z 3.0 to 11.2 at both ends. Of the four the critic attributed to the renderer, three are confirmed: the faceting is preview tessellation and there is no mesh deliverable, the blocky marking edges are raster magnification, and the flat white basin floor is a shading clip -- render_review brightens up to about 1.10x on directly-lit facets (the gray globe peaks at 224 against its 207 base), so a near-white filament at the brightest point of a camera-facing globe clamps at 255. The fourth guess is corrected: Mercury's base glyph really is two disconnected bars in the geometry, a seven-segment 1 lighting only segments b and c, each 1.00 by 0.80 mm with a 1.00 mm gap. That is the numeral this correction had to leave untouched, so it is disclosed rather than changed.
reviewer: independent native critic, given only the nine canonical images and no Wish, concept or product name; the unprimed read was recorded in full and fixed before the Wish was revealed
